html:
A slow-cooked stew of hominy maize, beans and cassava or sweet potato, with fish or meat, eaten all over Cape Verde and called its national dish.

Maize and beans came from the Americas through Portuguese ships and were grown on the dry islands from the 16th and 17th centuries, when the islands sat on the routes of the Atlantic slave trade. The poor version, cachupa pobre, was the food of hard years; the rich one has more meat. Leftovers fried for breakfast are cachupa guisada. It travels with the diaspora and appears at every family feast.
sum: A slow-cooked stew of hominy maize, beans and cassava or sweet potato, with fish or meat, eaten all over Cape Verde and called its national dish.
